asr.localModelHint: SenseVoice is fast and accurate for Chinese lectures. Qwen3-ASR is a bit more accurate and also handles English and 30+ other languages, so use it for English or heavily mixed lectures. On the CPU it is 2–3× slower than SenseVoice; turn on GPU acceleration to speed it up. If the chosen model isn't downloaded, another downloaded model is used.

settings.title: First, set up an LLM and speech recognition
settings.body: Speech recognition turns lectures into transcripts; the LLM writes notes, quizzes and answers. Click Next and we’ll walk you through Settings.

llm.title: LLM — DeepSeek as an example
llm.body: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama and Azure all work; pick a preset to fill in the protocol and endpoint, then fetch the model list.
llm.step1: Sign up on the <link>DeepSeek Platform</link> and create an API key (top up if your balance is low)
llm.step2: Pick the DeepSeek preset on the left and click Add; the Base URL is filled in as https://api.deepseek.com
llm.step3: Enter the API key, click Fetch models and pick one (context and reference pricing are shown), then Save

asr.title: Speech recognition — Volcengine or Alibaba Cloud
asr.body: Without it, on-device recognition is used (download SenseVoice for Chinese lectures). Cloud recognition doesn't use your computer's resources, and phones can only use the cloud.
asr.bodyMobile: Without it, pick "On-device" under Speech recognition and download SenseVoice (240 MB, works offline). Cloud recognition saves your phone's battery.
asr.volc: Volcengine: enable <link>Recording File Recognition (LLM)</link> to get an App ID and Access Token; set ASR backend to “Volcengine file transcription”, fill them in and click “Save Volcengine ASR credentials”
asr.aliyun: Alibaba Cloud: enable speech recognition in the Bailian console and create an API key (starts with sk-); set ASR backend to “Alibaba Cloud DashScope file transcription”, paste the key and click “Save Bailian API Key”

addCourse.title: Finally, create a course and import videos
addCourse.step1: Click “New Course Folder” and pick the folder that holds your lecture videos — they’re imported automatically
addCourse.step2: Inside a course, Import also takes local videos or Bilibili / YouTube links (the first Bilibili download asks for cookies.txt)
addCourse.step2Mobile: Inside a course, Import lets you pick videos from Photos or Files
addCourse.step3: Videos are transcribed, slides captured and notes written automatically — follow along in the processing queue

import.title: Bring in your videos
import.body: Upload local video or audio, or paste a Bilibili / YouTube link. Imports are transcribed and slides are captured automatically; with an LLM they become notes too.

findExplain.title: Snap a problem, find where it’s taught
findExplain.body: Snap a photo, paste a screenshot, or type the problem — it searches this course’s transcript and slides for where it’s explained, and can play those clips in order. Pasting an image on the course page works too.

concepts.title: Knowledge: this course’s concept map
concepts.body: Every concept pulled from the videos, with an explanation and where it’s taught; each one can be explained back with “Explain it to me” and gets a check once you do.

tabs.title: Your study materials live here
tabs.body: Once processing finishes, the overview, transcript and notes appear here; quizzes, slides and mind maps are under More.

notes.title: Press {{key}} to take a note
notes.body: The video pauses and the current timestamp is added to the end of your notes. Change the key in Settings → Shortcuts.

transcript.title: Select a line in the transcript
transcript.body: Highlight any text to ask AI about it, quote it to your notes, or make a cloze card.

assistant.title: Stuck? Ask the AI assistant
assistant.body: Click here (or press {{key}}). It has read this course’s transcript and slides, and timestamps in its answers are clickable. Turn on “Guide” and it won’t hand you the answer — it asks you step by step. Selecting a transcript line and choosing “Guide me through this” works too.
assistant.bodyTouch: Tap here. It has read this course’s transcript and slides, and timestamps in its answers are clickable. Turn on “Guide” and it won’t hand you the answer — it asks you step by step.

feynman.title: Explain it to find the gaps
feynman.body: In the Key chapters header, “Feynman explanation” lets you pick a chapter and explain it in your own words (speak or type). The AI checks only against the course text, shows what you missed or got wrong, and links back to the exact moment. You'll also get a gentle nudge when a chapter ends.

highlights.title: Speed up or skip the filler
highlights.body: Open Highlights in the player settings: the AI marks admin talk, chit-chat and repeated explanations. Speed them up or skip them, see how many minutes it saves, and undo anything it gets wrong.
highlights.bodyTouch: Tap the video to show the controls, then open Highlights in the settings: the AI marks admin talk, chit-chat and repeated explanations — speed them up or skip them, and it shows how many minutes it saves.

focus.title: Need to concentrate?
focus.body: Focus reading lets the study panel fill the workbench with the text centered while the video keeps playing. Press Esc to leave.

notesTouch.title: Jot a note as you watch
notesTouch.body: Tap Take a note in your notes: the video pauses and the current timestamp is added. With a keyboard, just press {{key}}.

findExplanation.title: Find the explanation
findExplanation.entryHint: Snap a problem or paste a screenshot to find where this course covers it
findExplanation.pickDesktop: Drop a screenshot of the problem here, or paste with ⌘V / Ctrl+V
findExplanation.pickMobile: Snap a problem, or pick one from your photos
findExplanation.typeInstead: No image? Type the problem instead
findExplanation.cropHint: If the page has several problems, drag to box the one you want.
findExplanation.checkText: Formulas and symbols are easy to misread — check before searching.
findExplanation.playInOrder: Play these {{count}} clips in order (~{{minutes}} min)
findExplanation.emptyTitle: Couldn't find this in the course
findExplanation.emptyDescription: It may not be covered, or the text wasn't recognized well. The assistant can work through it with you.

highlights.title: Highlights
highlights.generateHint: Let AI mark admin notes, chit-chat and repeats that you can speed through or skip

feynman.title: Explain it: {{topic}}
feynman.chapterPickerHint: Pick a chapter and explain it in your own words. I'll compare it with the captions and show what you missed.
feynman.prompt: Explain “{{topic}}” as if to a classmate who hasn't learned it. I'll compare it with the course and show what you covered and missed.
feynman.tapToSpeak: Tap to start, tap again when you're done
feynman.typeInstead: Can't talk right now? Type instead
feynman.placeholder: Explain it in your own words…

micError.denied: Microphone access was denied. Turn it on in system settings, or just type.
micError.unavailable: The microphone isn't available here — typing works just as well.
micError.failed: Recording failed. Try again or type.

feynman.filled: You filled {{count}} gap(s) from last time
feynman.allClear: Complete and accurate — nothing missed, nothing wrong.
feynman.makeCards: Make {{count}} review card(s) from the gaps
feynman.chapterEndText: Finished “{{chapter}}”? Explain it in your own words?
feynman.guidePrompt: When explaining “{{topic}}” I got this wrong: {{wrong}}. Don't tell me the answer — guide me step by step to see where I went wrong.
